t.6.30.1: Having spent that night there on Suvela, the heroic bulls among the monkeys beheld the forests and groves in Laṅkā.
t.6.30.2: Seeing those places, wholly gentle and delightful, broad and far-stretching, a delight to the eye, they were filled with wonder.
t.6.30.3: It was thick with campaka, aśoka, puṃnāga, sāla and tāla trees, overspread with groves of tamāla, and encircled by rows of nāga trees.
t.6.30.4: With hintāla, arjuna, nīpa and saptaparṇa trees in full blossom, and with tilaka, karṇikāra and pāṭala trees on every side.
t.6.30.5: Laṅkā shone with many kinds of divine trees, their tops in blossom and entwined with creepers, like Indra's Amarāvatī.
t.6.30.7: There the trees bear delightful flowers and fruits rich in fragrance, just as men wear ornaments.
t.6.30.6: It was adorned with trees bearing many-colored flowers and tender red shoots, with dark-green grassy meadows, and likewise with bright, varied rows of forest.
t.6.30.8: That forest, delightful and charming, resembling Caitraratha and like unto Nandana, bearing the flowers of all seasons and teeming with bees, shone in splendour.
t.6.30.9: At the forest waterfall, along with the water-hens and lapwings and the dancing peacocks, the call of the cuckoos was heard.
t.6.30.10: They were groves where the birds were ever in rapture, frequented by bees, their thickets thronged with cuckoos, and resounding with the calls of birds.
t.6.30.12: Then those heroic monkeys, able to take any form at will, thrilled and overjoyed, entered those forests and groves.
t.6.30.11: They are filled with the songs of bhṛṅgarāja birds and frequented by bees, resounding with the calls of koṇālaka birds and echoing with the cries of sārasa cranes.
t.6.30.13: As those mighty monkeys entered there, a breeze blew, fragrant from its contact with the flowers and pleasing to the sense of smell.
t.6.30.14: But other troop-leaders of the heroic monkeys, having come forth from the host and been given leave by Sugrīva, went to Laṅkā, adorned with banners.
t.6.30.15: With their own roars, those foremost among roarers terrified the birds, frightened the deer and elephants, and made that Laṅkā tremble.
t.6.30.17: Bears, lions and boars, buffaloes, elephants and deer, terrified by that sound, fled in fear to the ten directions.
t.6.30.16: Those beings of great speed made the earth suffer under their marching, and the dust kicked up by their feet suddenly rose high into the air.
t.6.30.18: And one peak of Trikūṭa, lofty and touching the sky, covered with flowers on every side, shone like gold.
t.6.30.20: That peak is hard for people to scale even in thought, let alone in deed; on that summit stands Laṅkā, protected by Rāvaṇa.
t.6.30.19: It stretches a hundred yojanas in extent, spotless and lovely to behold, smooth, splendid and vast, and hard to reach even for birds.
t.6.30.21: That city was adorned with lofty gateway towers resembling pale white clouds, and with a rampart of gold and of silver.
t.6.30.23: In which a palace adorned with a thousand pillars, shaped like the peak of Kailāsa, is seen as if scraping the sky.
t.6.30.22: Laṅkā was supremely adorned with palaces and lofty mansions, as the middle step of Viṣṇu, the sky, is adorned with clouds when the hot season has passed.
t.6.30.24: That caitya of the lord of the rākṣasas became the ornament of the city; it is guarded constantly by a full hundred rākṣasas.
t.6.30.25: Rāma, the elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa, glorious and accomplished in his aims, beheld together with the monkeys that prosperous city of Rāvaṇa.
t.6.30.26: Rāma, with his great army, beheld that city, filled with jewels and richly appointed, adorned with rows of palaces, its gates mighty and fitted with great engines.
